option_relations.rationale: Polymorphous light eruption does not match the specific clinical presentation and laboratory findings of the patient.
Polymorphic light eruption is another term for polymorphous light eruption and does not match the specific clinical presentation and laboratory findings of the patient.

The clinical presentation and laboratory findings of the patient, including the presence of parvovirus B19 DNA in lesional skin biopsy specimen, are consistent with Juvenile Spring Eruption (JSE) associated with parvovirus B19 infection.
Parvovirus B19-associated photodermatitis is a broader term that encompasses various skin manifestations associated with parvovirus B19 infection, including the patient's presentation.
